verifications.claim: Artemis III is currently targeted for launch in mid-2027, according to NASA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Launch Schedule Artemis III When 2027'; R3: 'the Artemis III mission... will be launched by mid-2027 as a low-Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: NASA source R1 targets 2027; R3 specifies mid-2027 matching the claim precisely.

verifications.claim: Artemis III will be a crewed mission aimed at testing rendezvous and docking capabilities with commercial landers in low-Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Artemis III demonstration mission in low Earth orbit will test one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin... to test rendezvous and docking capabilities between Orion and private commercial spacecraft'; R5: identical description
verifications.reasoning: Direct match to mission description in NASA sources.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, Artemis III launch date is scheduled for 2027.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'When 2027'; R3 (Feb 2026): 'launched by mid-2027'; timeline context from R2 (April 2026) post-Artemis II
verifications.reasoning: 2027 target supported around April 2026 timeline, but no source explicitly states 'as of April 2026'; broader confirmation.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, Artemis III crew will launch on the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket in the Orion spacecraft, as reported by Space.com.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The mission will launch crew in the Orion spacecraft on top of the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'; R5: 'The Artemis III crew will launch in Orion on the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'
verifications.reasoning: Exact details match NASA sources; timeline fits post-April 2026 context despite unattributed source.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, Artemis III crew will dock with a commercial lander such as SpaceX’s Starship in low-Earth orbit, as reported by Space.com.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R5: 'test rendezvous and docking capabilities between Orion and private commercial spacecraft... one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin'; R4: 'SpaceX Starship lunar lander'
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for docking with SpaceX commercial lander (Starship as example) in LEO; timeline fits.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, Artemis III mission does not include immediately landing on the Moon, as reported by Space.com.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R5: 'demonstration mission in low Earth orbit will test... rendezvous and docking... needed to land astronauts on the Moon' (no lunar landing); R3: 'Artemis III mission will no longer aim to land on the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm LEO-only test mission, no lunar landing.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, Artemis III mission revision follows concerns over technological readiness, notes SpaceNews and The Guardian.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3 (Guardian): 'radical changes... grapples with technical glitches... delays and technical problems... too risky'; R4 (SpaceNews): 'changing the scope of Artemis 3... if key elements suffer major delays... concern about... Starship'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match to named sources on concerns driving revision.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, Artemis III mission revision focuses on addressing delays in the human landing system (HLS).
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R3: 'technical glitches... delays... rethink its objectives for Artemis III'; R4: 'potential delays in hardware... SpaceX... Starship vehicle, including the lunar lander version that will be used on Artemis 3'
verifications.reasoning: Delays in lander/HLS (Starship) implied as key factor, but not exclusively 'focuses on HLS'; broader concerns.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, the actual human lunar landing has been shifted to the Artemis IV mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'The Artemis III mission will no longer aim to land on the moon... a new Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement of shift to Artemis IV.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, Artemis IV mission is targeted for 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'a new Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit target date for Artemis IV.
